title: Delicious Weeknight Pregnancy Menus: 5 Cook-Once Recipes
excerpt: Five flavorful recipes for busy evenings — soup, stir-fry, egg dishes and yogurt parfaits — balanced for protein, fiber and calcium.
content:
## Introduction
A healthy and balanced diet is crucial for pregnant women to ensure the well-being of both mother and baby. However, with busy schedules, many expectant mothers struggle to prepare nutritious and delicious meals. In this article, we will introduce 5 simple and tasty cook-once recipes, helping pregnant women enjoy healthy and balanced dinners.

## Nutrient Analysis
The recipes below are designed to provide a balanced amount of protein, fiber, and calcium, supporting the health of both mother and baby. According to the NHS, a balanced diet should include protein-rich foods like meat, fish, eggs, and dairy; fiber-rich foods like vegetables, fruits, and whole grains; and calcium-rich foods like dairy, leafy greens, and fortified plant-based milk.

## 5 Cook-Once Recipes
1. **Chicken and Vegetable Soup**: This simple and nutritious recipe includes chicken, vegetables, and broth. According to the CDC, chicken is an excellent source of protein, while vegetables provide fiber and essential vitamins.
2. **Beef and Vegetable Stir-Fry**: This recipe combines protein-rich beef with vegetables and spices, creating a balanced and delicious meal. According to the ACOG, beef is an excellent source of iron, helping to prevent anemia in pregnant women.
3. **Eggs and Vegetable Salad**: This simple recipe includes eggs, vegetables, and whole grains, providing a balanced mix of protein, fiber, and calcium. According to the NIH ODS, eggs are an excellent source of folate, helping to prevent birth defects of the brain and spine.
4. **Yogurt and Fruit Parfait**: This recipe combines calcium-rich yogurt with fruit and granola, creating a delicious and balanced dessert. According to the FDA, yogurt is an excellent source of calcium, supporting the development of the baby's bones and teeth.
5. **Cheese and Vegetable Frittata**: This simple recipe includes cheese, vegetables, and whole grains, providing a balanced mix of protein, fiber, and calcium. According to the WHO, cheese is an excellent source of calcium, supporting the development of the baby's bones and teeth.

## Practical Tips
To enjoy healthy and balanced dinners, pregnant women should:
* Choose fresh and nutritious ingredients
* Read food labels to avoid additives and preservatives
* Cook at home to control salt and sugar intake
* Stay hydrated and limit sugary drinks

## When to Seek Help
If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about their diet or health, they should consult their doctor or a registered dietitian. According to the NHS, pregnant women should consult their doctor before making any significant changes to their diet.

## Sources
* WHO: Healthy diet during pregnancy — https://www.who.int/tools/elena/interventions/nutrition-pregnancy
* NHS: Foods to avoid in pregnancy — https://www.nhs.uk/pregnancy/keeping-well/foods-to-avoid/

* NIH ODS: Folate — Fact Sheet for Health Professionals — https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Folate-HealthProfessional/
* FDA: Advice about Eating Fish — https://www.fda.gov/food/consumers/advice-about-eating-fish
